$comment: Translation POLICY, not translation data. Consumed by the i18n guard tests. Keep flat catalogs (<lang>.json) free of metadata so any TMS can read them directly.

englishOnly.$comment: Deliberately English in every language: full sentences where a machine translation is worse than an honest English fallback. A native reviewer must do these by hand. Guard tests assert NO language block defines them.

reviewPending.$comment: Domains whose non-English strings are machine-drafted and still awaiting native review.

$passes.$comment: A CONSISTENCY pass ran 2026-08-15, then a VOCABULARY pass the same day. Both are machine passes, not native ones, and the status fields below deliberately still say 'awaiting native review'. What could be checked mechanically was fixed: register conformance, glossary term conformance, placeholder/newline/markdown parity, and the keys a locale was missing. What could NOT be checked is whether the prose is any good, which is why a native pass is still owed. `npm run i18n:review` re-runs the mechanical half.
fixed2026-08-15: fr: 88 strings were in the tu register in a vous catalog — 64 with tu pronouns/possessives and 24 tu-imperatives ('Choisis un fichier image'). Now 0.
es: register verified clean, 0 usted forms.

es 25 + fr 16 keys had translated a do-not-translate term (PR→récord, Reps→repeticiones, Capsule→cápsula, Coach→entrenador). The catalog majority kept the English term in every case, so the minority was the defect.
The Plans/meal-planner keys were translated concurrently by the session that built the feature (2e11b6b9); that work is theirs and was kept as-is on rebase. It passes every check in this pass.

fr: BOTH vocabulary collisions are now resolved. Streak was 'Série', the same word as Set, across 128 strings; it is now 'Flamme' (kegan asked for this explicitly after first choosing to leave it open). Chosen on the app's own iconography — StreakFlame.jsx, 82 Flame references, 8 French strings already using the flame emoji — not on taste. See _glossary.json $streakNote and $setNote.
openQuestions: NOTHING vocabulary-level is open. Both collisions found on 2026-08-15 were settled: es Regimen → 'Programa', fr Streak → 'Flamme'. `npm run i18n:review` now passes clean, and it goes red on a NEW collision rather than re-reporting a documented one.

What remains for a native reviewer is the PROSE, which no tool here can judge. Highest value first: coach.* (the longest copy in the app, and where a mistranslated training cue costs the most), then onboarding.*, then the notification bodies. Read _glossary.json before the catalog.

Still deliberately untranslated in every locale: the 19 englishOnly keys (a guard test fails if a non-English block defines one) and cardio.type.swimming_* / cardio.modes.swimming, which cardioTypeLabel holds for a native pass specifically.
$passes.echoNote: Enforcing doNotTranslate RAISES englishEcho, which _coverage.json's ratchet reads as a regression. Six keys moved that way on purpose (es shop.*Capsule.name ×3; fr common.reps, workout.templates.reps, weeklyMealPlannerModal.title). The two guards genuinely disagree here; the glossary wins and the baseline is regenerated.

vocabularyDecisions2026-08-15.es.Regimen: Régimen/Rutina → Programa (47 keys). 'Rutina' also meant Routine; 'Régimen' reads dietary.
vocabularyDecisions2026-08-15.fr.Streak: Série → Flamme (60 keys). 'Série' also meant Set, and cannot move — it is the standard term for a training set.

fixed2026-08-16: pt taken 1,486 → 3,796 keys (38.9% → 99.4%), matching es and fr exactly. 2,310 strings across 13 batches, every one through the placeholder/newline/markdown validator, which refuses a whole batch rather than writing a partial one.
All 11 onboarding accentWord keys asserted to be a single token hitting exactly one word of their pt heading — the bug that shipped in Spanish as 'en serio' and was caught only by a screenshot.
Gym was split 2 academia / 3 ginásio; ginásio is a sports hall in Brazil, so those three were corrected with the gender change they force (ao ginásio → à academia).

spanish.$comment: The whole Spanish catalog is a machine draft produced 2026-08-14, consistent with _glossary.json (tú register, 49 fixed terms) and verified for placeholder, newline and markdown parity. A second machine consistency pass ran 2026-08-15 (see $passes). It has still NOT had a native pass. A reviewer should read _glossary.json first, then work namespace by namespace — coach.* and onboarding.* carry the long-form coaching prose and are where a wrong register or a mistranslated cue costs the most.

french.$comment: The whole French catalog is a machine draft produced 2026-08-14, consistent with _glossary.json — register VOUS, which is the opposite of Spanish — and verified for placeholder, newline and markdown parity. A second machine consistency pass ran 2026-08-15 (see $passes) and moved 88 strings out of the tu register. Still NOT natively reviewed. Read _glossary.json first; it also records that the translation uses 'Série' for both Streak and Set, which a native pass should settle.

portuguese.$comment: The whole Portuguese catalog is a machine draft completed 2026-08-16, taken from 38.9% to 99.4% — the same coverage es and fr sit at. It is pt-BR: measured, not assumed, on the 1,486 strings that already shipped (99 Brazilian markers against 6 European). Register is Brazilian UI voice — no explicit pronoun, você-form imperatives, seu/sua possessives. Consistent with _glossary.json's pt block (49 terms, derived from those same shipped strings) and verified for placeholder, newline and markdown parity on every key. It has NOT had a native pass. A reviewer should read _glossary.json first, then work namespace by namespace — coach.* is 314 keys of long-form coaching prose and onboarding.* another 219, and those are where a wrong register or a mistranslated cue costs the most.
portuguese.$driftFound: 37 Plans strings had arrived in EUROPEAN Portuguese and in the tu register — 'à tua alimentação', 'Configura', 'Substitui', 'Registá-la', and 'para alimentares o esforço e recuperares' (the personal infinitive, which pt-BR does not use that way) — against 3,759 Brazilian ones. Corrected, and i18n-review.mjs now carries pt register rules so the class is caught rather than found by eye.

machineTranslated.$comment: Keys drafted by machine, pending native review.

domains.$comment: Key prefixes grouping the catalog into reviewable domains. Replaces the old one-part-file-per-domain layout: the guard tests slice the flat catalogs by these prefixes. A prefix list is also the natural unit to hand a translator.

released.$comment: Locales the app OFFERS in the picker. Authoritative list is SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES in src/lib/i18n.js; this records the decision and why. A locale joins when it is COMPLETE, not when it is started.

shelved.$comment: Have catalogs in src/locales/ and are still guarded by _coverage.json and the DEV checker, but are not offered. Shelved 2026-08-13 at ~49% of the English catalog: half a translated screen reads as a broken app, where an absent language reads as a decision. No account had ever selected one. Finishing all fourteen is ~135,000 words, roughly $16k of professional post-editing.
shelved.termPass2026-08-16: The six LATIN-SCRIPT shelved locales had the same do-not-translate defect es and fr did, and it is now fixed: de 40, pt 29, it 33, pl 47, nl 19, tr 74 keys where a term the glossary keeps in English had been translated (Reps→Wiederholungen/powtórzeń/tekrar, Capsule→Kapsel/kapsuła/Kapsül, PR→Rekord/rekor, Coach→Trener/Koç, Cardio→Kardiyo). All six now check clean. This is term CONSISTENCY only — it says nothing about whether the prose is good, and these locales remain shelved at ~38% coverage. Inflection was handled per language: Polish declines the loanword (Zapytaj Coacha) and Turkish suffixes it with the apostrophe foreign nouns take, harmonised to the loanword's own vowels (Cardio'yu, Coach'a, Capsule'ü, PR'ı) — that suffixation is the part most worth a native check if any of these is ever released.
shelved.notCheckedAndWhy: The six NON-LATIN shelved locales — ja ko zh ar hi ru — were NOT touched. They keep these terms by TRANSLITERATING them (カーディオ is Cardio, ストリーク is streak), which a Latin-script matcher cannot tell from a translation; it reported 485 findings across them that were nearly all wrong. `npm run i18n:review` now marks those rows as candidates rather than failures. Deciding them needs the expected katakana/hangul/Cyrillic form per term recorded in _glossary.json, which is only worth doing if one of those locales is released.
